record.title: Google DeepMind reports a human-steered Antigravity workflow for antimicrobial-peptide candidate search
record.summary: Google DeepMind’s 15 October walkthrough describes a researcher-steered Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash workflow that searches UniProt candidates, cross-checks sequence similarity, compares predicted structures and genomic context, and prepares a wet-lab protocol. The example names UniProt A0A0U0D591, a 97-amino-acid protein assigned to the Lactococcin 972 family; the company says the candidate and others are undergoing wet-lab validation. This is a first-party account of a computational candidate-selection workflow, not evidence of antibacterial efficacy or independent discovery performance.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google DeepMind reports that a researcher and Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash used UniProt search, Swiss-Prot sequence comparison, AlphaFold/Foldseek structural comparison, genomic-neighborhood analysis and literature synthesis to prioritize UniProt A0A0U0D591 as a possible antimicrobial peptide candidate.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google DeepMind says this candidate and several others from the same workflow are undergoing wet-lab validation; no results from those tests are reported in the inspected post.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The source does not establish antibacterial activity, toxicity, target engagement, improved discovery yield, faster search than a human-led baseline, or reproducible end-to-end scientific autonomy.

evidence_gaps.description: The proposed antimicrobial activity, toxicity and target engagement of A0A0U0D591 have not been established in the inspected source; the source says wet-lab validation is underway but reports no data.
The company describes days of fragmented triage becoming a single session but gives no measured task time, candidate yield, error rate or human-led baseline.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently validated, a human-steered agent workflow that links protein-sequence search, structural comparison, genomic context and planned bench tests could change parts of early antimicrobial discovery. The single company-reported example does not establish antimicrobial activity, discovery yield or general workflow efficiency.
limitations: Evidence is a single first-party product walkthrough; the research desk did not run the workflow or inspect model, database-query or analysis artifacts.
The identified protein is a candidate only. Predicted function, structural similarity and genomic context do not establish antimicrobial activity.
The post says wet-lab validation is in progress but provides no susceptibility, toxicity, target-engagement or replication results.
The walkthrough is human-steered: the researcher sets the goal, chooses evidence to collect and guides analysis; it does not demonstrate autonomous research.
No matched baseline or quantitative data support the company's qualitative description of days of triage being compressed to one session.

The example names UniProt A0A0U0D591, a 97-amino-acid protein assigned to the Lactococcin 972 family; the company says the candidate and others are undergoing wet-lab validation. This is a first-party account of a computational candidate-selection workflow, not evidence of antibacterial efficacy or independent discovery performance.

technical.claimed_result: Google DeepMind reports one candidate search in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae and says the lead plus several other candidates are being wet-lab validated. No experimental outcome is yet reported in the inspected post.
technical.compute_or_cost: No model usage, compute cost, experiment cost or staff-time measurements are reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary page demonstrates that Google DeepMind publicly described this workflow and candidate. the research desk did not verify the underlying biological result, execute the tools, or independently reproduce the analysis.
technical.mechanism: The reported human-steered workflow combines ProtNLM-based sequence/function search over UniProt, Swiss-Prot comparison via BLAST, predicted-structure retrieval and Foldseek comparison, genomic-neighborhood reasoning, literature synthesis, and generation of a proposed wet-lab protocol. The researcher selects the goal, directs evidence collection and iterates with the agent.
technical.regime: One walkthrough focused on a narrow amino-acid window in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae. The page identifies UniProt A0A0U0D591 as a 97-amino-acid Lactococcin 972-family bacteriocin candidate. No broader dataset, baseline, yield, time or error-rate evaluation is given.
technical.reproducibility: Not assessed by the research desk. No workflow code, prompt trace, full query log, data snapshot or wet-lab results were inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched human-led, conventional-tool, or alternative-agent baseline is reported.

brief.title: Google DeepMind reports a human-steered Antigravity workflow for antimicrobial-peptide candidate search
brief.why_it_matters: Early antimicrobial discovery can require fragmented sequence, structure, genomic and literature tools. If independently validated, a human-steered agent that coordinates these steps could help biologists prioritize candidates for experiments. The post reports one example and says wet-lab validation is pending; it gives no independent comparison of search time, candidate yield, biological activity or downstream clinical value.
